# scheduler

	import "github.com/caimlas/meept/internal/scheduler"

Package scheduler provides cron\-based job scheduling for the meept daemon.

Package scheduler — rewake.go is the timer→rewake adapter: it bridges scheduler job completion onto the EXISTING hook.async\_rewake topic that the agent loop's rewake consumer is already subscribed to. It is not a new bus topic: the topic literal mirrors internal/agent's HookAsyncRewakeTopic \(the agent package owns the const; importing it from scheduler would invert the layering the leaf spec fixes: agent must stay scheduler\-agnostic\).

Session mapping: scheduler jobs carry no conversation/session identity \(a timer fires for the daemon, not for one chat\), so the published payload has an empty session\_id. Per the loop\_rewake contract, empty session\_id is a broadcast — every loop with an armed consumer wakes. This is the correct behavior for timer completion: any active loop may need to react to a job finishing.

<a name="DefaultClaimRetentionDays"></a>DefaultClaimRetentionDays is the default retention for claimed ticks.

<a name="DefaultJobResultOutputBytes"></a>DefaultJobResultOutputBytes is the bounded window job\_status reads back from a spill file on demand.

<a name="DefaultOneShotCatchUpWindow"></a>DefaultOneShotCatchUpWindow mirrors config.DefaultOneShotWindow \(2h\). It is only a fallback: the live window always comes from the scheduler's cfg.Scheduler.OneShotWindow via effectiveOneShotWindow.

	const DefaultOneShotCatchUpWindow = 2 * time.Hour

<a name="DeliveryHistoryRetentionDays"></a>DeliveryHistoryRetentionDays bounds the per\-job delivery history age.

	const DeliveryHistoryRetentionDays = 30

<a name="HookAsyncRewakeTopic"></a>HookAsyncRewakeTopic is the EXISTING rewake bus topic consumed by the agent loop \(internal/agent.HookAsyncRewakeTopic\). Duplicated as a literal to preserve package layering; a test pins both spellings equal.

	const HookAsyncRewakeTopic = "hook.async_rewake"

<a name="MaxDeliveryHistoryRecords"></a>MaxDeliveryHistoryRecords bounds the per\-job delivery history length.

	const MaxDeliveryHistoryRecords = 200

<a name="MaxSpillBytes"></a>MaxSpillBytes caps the stdout/stderr spill file per execution attempt. Writes past the cap are dropped \(the writer keeps consuming so the child never blocks on a full pipe\) and the settled result is marked truncated.

	const MaxSpillBytes = int64(64) << 20 // 64 MiB
	

<a name="MinTimingEverySeconds"></a>MinTimingEverySeconds is the floor for the \`every\` kind, mirroring the dsh MIN\_EVERY\_INTERVAL\_SECONDS constraint. Higher\-frequency recurrences are rejected as frequency\_too\_high.

	const MinTimingEverySeconds = 60

<a name="NotifyJobComplete"></a>
## func NotifyJobComplete

	func NotifyJobComplete(publish func(topic string, msg *models.BusMessage) int, msg *models.BusMessage) int

NotifyJobComplete publishes a hook.async\_rewake signal with Source=timer so any armed agent loop wakes at its next iteration boundary. No mid\-turn interrupt: the rewake consumer buffers the signal and injectRewakes delivers it as a system note.

publish is injectable for tests \(pass nil to treat it as a no\-op\). msg, if non\-nil, is published to HookAsyncRewakeTopic via publish; the scheduler calls this from its single central job\-completion site so every job type \(agent/shell/reminder/…, cron and RunNow alike\) rewakes the daemon.

<a name="RegisterTiming"></a>
## func RegisterTiming

	func RegisterTiming(c *cron.Cron, cfg JobConfig, job Job, oneShotWindow time.Duration) (cron.EntryID, error)

RegisterTiming registers cfg's Timing spec on the given cron engine in the engine's location so cron.WithLocation DST handling applies. \`at\` specs register as a one\-shot entry that removes itself after firing exactly once. oneShotWindow is the configured scheduling horizon for the at\-kind rejection; callers without a scheduler pass DefaultOneShotCatchUpWindow.

This standalone form has no claim store or jobs.json writer available, so its one\-shot closure executes directly; the scheduler\-backed registerTiming \(RegisterTimingVia\) is the production path and delivers through fireOneShotOnce.

<a name="SweepAgedJobSpills"></a>
## func SweepAgedJobSpills

	func SweepAgedJobSpills(now time.Time, horizon time.Duration) (int, error)

SweepAgedJobSpills deletes spill files under $MEEPT\_HOME/spill/jobs older than the result\-lane horizon. The lane keeps at most resultLaneCap entries and prunes claims at DefaultClaimRetentionDays, so a spill older than that horizon can no longer have a lane entry reading it: crash\-orphaned files \(a result never settled, a lane entry evicted while the daemon was down, or a PutResult that crashed before its best\-effort delete\) are unreferenced garbage. Called at scheduler Start, not per\-run — cheap at boot, and it needs no synchronization with in\-flight writes.

The horizon follows the claim retention so one knob stays consistent across the scheduler's boot\-time sweeps.

<a name="DeliveryHistory"></a>
## type DeliveryHistory

DeliveryHistory is a bounded, most\-recent\-first\-kept history of delivery receipts for one schedule.

	type DeliveryHistory struct {
	    Records              []ScheduleDeliveryReceipt `json:"records"`
	    EarlierRecordsPruned bool                      `json:"earlier_records_pruned"`
	
	    // LastEvictedStuckIDs carries the MessageIDs of any pending/in_flight
	    // rows evicted by the most recent Append as a last-resort count-bound
	    // eviction (bughunt 2026-11-12 F4). The caller (recordDelivery) Warns
	    // naming each so the lost occurrence is at least observable. Empty
	    // when the last Append evicted only terminal rows (or nothing).
	    LastEvictedStuckIDs []string `json:"last_evicted_stuck_ids,omitempty"`
	}

<a name="DeliveryHistory.Append"></a>
### func \(\*DeliveryHistory\) Append

	func (h *DeliveryHistory) Append(r ScheduleDeliveryReceipt)

Append adds a receipt and enforces the retention bounds: records older than DeliveryHistoryRetentionDays \(measured on DeliveredAt, falling back to ScheduledAt\) and records beyond the MaxDeliveryHistoryRecords most recent are dropped. Any drop sets EarlierRecordsPruned.

Non\-terminal statuses \(pending/in\_flight\) are EXEMPT from the age prune \(bughunt 2026\-11\-10 B8\): recoverInFlightDeliveries re\-delivers FROM pending/in\_flight rows, so pruning a stuck receipt older than retention permanently lost the tick it represents. Age\-retention is for delivered history only; a stuck row survives until recovery resolves it.

The count bound evicts TERMINAL rows \(delivered/failed\) first. A stuck row is evicted only as a last resort — when the bound still overflows with nothing terminal left — and that case is flagged so the caller can Warn naming the MessageID \(bughunt 2026\-11\-12 F4\): silently evicting a pending/in\_flight row loses the occurrence it represents.

<a name="DeliveryStatus"></a>
## type DeliveryStatus

DeliveryStatus is the lifecycle state of a scheduled\-message delivery.

	type DeliveryStatus string

<a name="DeliveryPending"></a>

	const (
	    // DeliveryPending: the occurrence is due but dispatch has not started.
	    DeliveryPending DeliveryStatus = "pending"
	    // DeliveryInFlight: dispatched (or about to be) but not yet acked by the
	    // target session. A crash here is recoverable via re-delivery.
	    DeliveryInFlight DeliveryStatus = "in_flight"
	    // DeliveryDelivered: the publish to chat.request succeeded.
	    DeliveryDelivered DeliveryStatus = "delivered"
	)

<a name="ExecutionOptions"></a>
## type ExecutionOptions

ExecutionOptions carries per\-delivery context from the dispatch boundary into executeJob.

	type ExecutionOptions struct {
	    // Tick is the scheduled tick being delivered. Zero means unknown

	    // MissedCount is the number of ticks coalesced into this delivery

<a name="Job"></a>
## type Job

Job represents a schedulable task.

	type Job interface {
	    // ID returns the unique identifier for this job.
	    ID() string
	    // Name returns a human-readable name for this job.
	    Name() string
	    // Schedule returns the cron expression for this job.
	    Schedule() string
	    // Execute runs the job with the given context.
	    Execute(ctx context.Context) error
	    // Type returns the job type (agent, shell, reminder).
	    Type() JobType
	    // Config returns the job configuration for persistence.
	    Config() JobConfig
	}

<a name="CreateJob"></a>
### func CreateJob

	func CreateJob(cfg JobConfig, msgBus *bus.MessageBus) (Job, error)

CreateJob creates a job from a JobConfig using only the message bus. For extended job types \(optimization, security, learning\), use CreateJobWithDeps.

<a name="CreateJobWithDeps"></a>
### func CreateJobWithDeps

	func CreateJobWithDeps(cfg JobConfig, deps *JobDependencies) (Job, error)

CreateJobWithDeps creates a job from a JobConfig with full dependencies.

<a name="JobConfig"></a>
## type JobConfig

JobConfig is the serializable configuration for a job.

	type JobConfig struct {
	    ID        string            `json:"id"`
	    Name      string            `json:"name"`
	    Type      JobType           `json:"type"`
	    Schedule  string            `json:"schedule"`
	    Enabled   bool              `json:"enabled"`
	    CreatedAt time.Time         `json:"created_at"`
	    LastRunAt *time.Time        `json:"last_run_at,omitempty"`
	    LastError string            `json:"last_error,omitempty"`
	    RunCount  int64             `json:"run_count"`
	    Tags      []string          `json:"tags,omitempty"`
	    Metadata  map[string]string `json:"metadata,omitempty"`
	
	    // Type-specific configuration
	    AgentConfig        *AgentJobConfig        `json:"agent_config,omitempty"`
	    ShellConfig        *ShellJobConfig        `json:"shell_config,omitempty"`
	    ReminderConfig     *ReminderJobConfig     `json:"reminder_config,omitempty"`
	    OptimizationConfig *OptimizationJobConfig `json:"optimization_config,omitempty"`
	    SecurityConfig     *SecurityJobConfig     `json:"security_config,omitempty"`
	    LearningConfig     *LearningJobConfig     `json:"learning_config,omitempty"`
	
	    // Timing is the semantic schedule spec (leaf 05-schedule/01-timing-kinds).
	    // When set, the job may be expressed and re-registered from this spec
	    // (Schedule OR Timing validation); the normalized cron string stays in
	    // Schedule for the engine.
	    Timing *TimingSpec `json:"timing,omitempty"`
	
	    // One-shot (TimingAt) lifecycle bookkeeping. Additive JSON fields:
	    // older rows without them load unchanged and behave as today.
	    // OneShotFailed marks a one-shot whose due time fell outside the
	    // [scheduler] one_shot_window catch-up horizon before the daemon could
	    // fire it — the job never ran, the row stops looking schedulable (no
	    // cron entry), and it stays re-runnable via RunNow. OneShotFiredAt
	    // records when a boot-recovered overdue one-shot fired, so the boot
	    // sweep neither re-fires nor re-marks it.
	    OneShotFailed  bool       `json:"one_shot_failed,omitempty"`
	    OneShotFiredAt *time.Time `json:"one_shot_fired_at,omitempty"`
	
	    // Delivery bookkeeping (leaf 05-schedule/02-delivery-inbox). Both are
	    // optional and only populated for jobs that deliver to a session inbox.
	    LastDelivery    *ScheduleDeliveryReceipt `json:"last_delivery,omitempty"`
	    DeliveryHistory *DeliveryHistory         `json:"delivery_history,omitempty"`
	}

MarshalJSON implements json.Marshaler for JobConfig.

<a name="JobDependencies"></a>
## type JobDependencies

JobDependencies holds dependencies for extended job types.

	type JobDependencies struct {
	    Bus              *bus.MessageBus
	    MemoryManager    MemoryOptimizer
	    LearningPipeline LearningConsolidator
	    SecurityEngine   SecurityScanner
	
	    // Guard is the two-phase execution-time fence for shell jobs. Nil skips
	    // guard checks (legacy construction paths and standalone tests).
	    Guard ShellCommandGuard
	    // ResultSink receives settled shell-job execution results (the result
	    // lane). Nil skips the lane.
	    ResultSink ResultSink
	}

<a name="JobExecutionResult"></a>
## type JobExecutionResult

JobExecutionResult is a settled execution attempt in the scheduler's result lane. Output is NOT stored here: it spills to a file under $MEEPT\_HOME/spill/jobs/\<handle\>.out and this row only keeps the small bookkeeping needed to find and bound it. Keys are JobID \(the handle\); a recurring job's successive runs overwrite by design \(job\_status takes only a handle, so it can only report the latest attempt\).

	type JobExecutionResult struct {
	    JobID        string    `json:"job_id"`
	    ExitCode     int       `json:"exit_code"`
	    Status       string    `json:"status"`
	    StartedAt    time.Time `json:"started_at"`
	    FinishedAt   time.Time `json:"finished_at"`
	    OutputPath   string    `json:"output_path,omitempty"`
	    OutputBytes  int64     `json:"output_bytes,omitempty"`
	    OutputSHA256 string    `json:"output_sha256,omitempty"`
	    // TruncatedTo is reserved for a bounded inline view. The file-backed
	    // lane never truncates the spill file, so writers leave it at 0;
	    // readers report how many bytes they actually returned.
	    TruncatedTo int64  `json:"truncated_to,omitempty"`
	    Error       string `json:"error,omitempty"`
	}

## type Option

Option is a functional option for configuring the Scheduler.

<a name="WithClaimRetentionDays"></a>
### func WithClaimRetentionDays

	func WithClaimRetentionDays(days int) Option

WithClaimRetentionDays sets the claimed\-tick retention window \(scheduler claim\_retention\_days\). Claims older than this are pruned on startup. Non\-positive values fall back to DefaultClaimRetentionDays \(7\).

<a name="WithCoalesceMissed"></a>
### func WithCoalesceMissed

	func WithCoalesceMissed(enabled bool) Option

WithCoalesceMissed controls missed\-tick coalescing \(scheduler coalesce\_missed\). Default true: after downtime, only the latest due tick per job is delivered once, with missed\_count metadata. Set false to restore the accumulate\-each behavior \(one delivery per missed tick\).

<a name="Scheduler.CancelJob"></a>
### func \(\*Scheduler\) CancelJob

	func (s *Scheduler) CancelJob(handle, reason string) (status string, stopped bool, exitCode int, err error)

CancelJob cancels the in\-flight execution for handle, waits a 2s grace for it to settle, then escalates to a process\-group kill. It is idempotent: an already\-settled handle returns "already\_done" as a successful no\-op.

status is one of "cancelled"/"succeeded"/"failed" \(settled\), "already\_done" or "not\_found". stopped reports whether an in\-flight run was actually cancelled. exitCode is the settled exit code when available.

### func \(\*Scheduler\) ClaimTick

	func (s *Scheduler) ClaimTick(jobID string, tick time.Time) (claimed bool, err error)

ClaimTick atomically claims a tick for a job before delivery. It returns false without error when the tick was already claimed \(constraint violation\), which marks it delivered — callers must skip dispatch.

<a name="Scheduler.ProcessMissedTicks"></a>
### func \(\*Scheduler\) ProcessMissedTicks

	func (s *Scheduler) ProcessMissedTicks(now time.Time) ([]MissedTickRun, error)

ProcessMissedTicks computes due ticks per job since lastWake and delivers them. With coalesce\_missed enabled \(default\) only the latest tick per job is delivered, once, with missed\_count metadata logged at info level; disabled, every due tick is delivered individually. lastWake is advanced to now after the sweep.

The scheduler must be running. Call this once at startup \(Start does this automatically\) or after known downtime; cron fires continue to use the claim\-before\-deliver path, so double delivery cannot occur either way.

### func \(\*Scheduler\) PutResult

PutResult writes a settled result into the scheduler's result lane. Exported for crash\-recovery callers \(markOneShotFailed\) and CancelJob's synthetic cancelled result.

### func \(\*Scheduler\) RegisterTimingVia

	func (s *Scheduler) RegisterTimingVia(cfg JobConfig, job Job) (cron.EntryID, error)

RegisterTimingVia registers a Timing\-carrying JobConfig on the scheduler's engine \(DST\-safe: the engine's location applies\). Used from ScheduleConfig and loadPersistedJobs so a persisted Timing re\-registers on restart.

<a name="ShellCommandGuard"></a>
## type ShellCommandGuard

ShellCommandGuard is the two\-phase execution\-time fence for shell jobs. Phase 1 \(CheckCommand\) is risk/permission classification and runs before work\-dir resolution; phase 2 \(CheckCommandInDir\) is the fence/Tirith/ network\-class check and runs after resolution. Both must run BEFORE the command is spawned. The sibling security leaf implements this interface; this package deliberately does not reimplement risk logic.

	type ShellCommandGuard interface {
	    CheckCommand(command string) error
	    CheckCommandInDir(ctx context.Context, command, workDir string) error
	}

<a name="ShellJob.Execute"></a>
### func \(\*ShellJob\) Execute

	func (j *ShellJob) Execute(ctx context.Context) error

Execute runs the shell command.

SECURITY NOTE: execution\-time guarding is implemented here via the optional ShellCommandGuard \(both phases run BEFORE the command is spawned\). The creation\-time fence check lives in tool\_schedule\_create.go; there is a TOCTOU window between creation and execution where the working directory or referenced files could change. The daemon wires the guard through JobDependencies so every scheduler\-fired shell job is re\-checked at execution time. Standalone construction \(tests, tooling\) leaves it nil and skips the check, preserving the legacy behavior.

<a name="ShellJobConfig"></a>
## type ShellJobConfig

ShellJobConfig holds configuration for shell jobs.

	type ShellJobConfig struct {
	    Command    string            `json:"command"`
	    Args       []string          `json:"args,omitempty"`
	    WorkDir    string            `json:"work_dir,omitempty"`
	    Env        map[string]string `json:"env,omitempty"`
	    Timeout    time.Duration     `json:"timeout,omitempty"`
	    CaptureOut bool              `json:"capture_output"`
	    // GuardCommand is the command string checked by the execution-time
	    // guard. When set, it MUST be the full shell source that command/args
	    // will execute (job_start sets it to the user command when command is
	    // /bin/sh and args are ["-c", <user command>]). Empty falls back to
	    // Command for legacy shell jobs.
	    //
	    // TRUST BOUNDARY: GuardCommand is legacy persistence data, never
	    // trusted over what actually executes. newShellJob derives the guard
	    // source from command/args for the /bin/sh -c X wrapper shape and
	    // ignores a mismatched field (warn-logged), so a persisted row cannot
	    // present "echo harmless" to the guard while "evil" executes.
	    GuardCommand string `json:"guard_command,omitempty"`
	}

<a name="TimingKind"></a>
## type TimingKind

TimingKind is the semantic kind of a model\-authored timing spec.

	type TimingKind string

<a name="TimingRRule"></a>The five semantic timing kinds \(L1 contract\). The constants keep the Go\-side names used across the scheduler \(switch statements, tests\); the JSON WIRE shape is the contracted snake\_case form \(TimingSpec.MarshalJSON\): "rrule", "daily", "weekly", "at", "every".

	const (
	    TimingRRule  TimingKind = "TimingRRule"
	    TimingDaily  TimingKind = "TimingDaily"
	    TimingWeekly TimingKind = "TimingWeekly"
	    TimingAt     TimingKind = "TimingOneShot"
	    TimingEvery  TimingKind = "TimingEvery"
	)

<a name="TimingSpec"></a>
## type TimingSpec

TimingSpec is the semantic timing layer over the robfig/cron engine. A persisted JobConfig keeps its normalized cron \`Schedule\` string for the engine and carries this spec for semantic re\-registration on restart.

	type TimingSpec struct {
	    Kind     TimingKind    `json:"kind"`
	    Time     string        `json:"time,omitempty"`      // HH:mm:ss (daily/weekly)
	    TimeZone string        `json:"time_zone,omitempty"` // IANA (daily/weekly/rrule DTSTART TZID)
	    Weekdays []int         `json:"weekdays,omitempty"`  // ISO 1=Mon..7=Sun, ascending unique (weekly)
	    At       *time.Time    `json:"at,omitempty"`        // absolute instant (at)
	    Every    time.Duration `json:"every,omitempty"`     // >= MinTimingEverySeconds (every)
	    RRule    string        `json:"rrule,omitempty"`     // "DTSTART;TZID=<IANA>:<ts>\nRRULE:<rule>" (rrule)
	}

<a name="ParseTiming"></a>
### func ParseTiming

	func ParseTiming(spec string) (*TimingSpec, error)

ParseTiming parses a model\-facing timing spec string into a TimingSpec.

Supported forms:

	daily <HH:mm[:ss]> [<IANA tz>]
	weekly <DOW-list> <HH:mm[:ss]> [<IANA tz>]   (DOW names or ISO numbers)
	at <RFC3339>
	every <Go duration>
	rrule:\nDTSTART;TZID=<IANA>:<yyyymmddThhmmss>\nRRULE:<rule>
	

<a name="TimingSpec.CronExpr"></a>
### func \(\*TimingSpec\) CronExpr

	func (t *TimingSpec) CronExpr() (string, error)

CronExpr returns the robfig/cron expression for this spec \(6\-field, second\-precision form matching the scheduler engine's parser; \`every\` yields an @every descriptor\).

<a name="TimingSpec.MarshalJSON"></a>
### func \(TimingSpec\) MarshalJSON

	func (t TimingSpec) MarshalJSON() ([]byte, error)

MarshalJSON serializes the spec with the kind in the contracted snake\_case wire form \("rrule"/"daily"/"weekly"/"at"/"every"\), never the Go\-side constants \("TimingOneShot" etc.\). All other fields use the struct tags verbatim.

<a name="TimingSpec.NextOccurrence"></a>
### func \(\*TimingSpec\) NextOccurrence

	func (t *TimingSpec) NextOccurrence(from time.Time) (time.Time, bool)

NextOccurrence resolves the next wall\-clock occurrence at or after \`from\`, DST\-safe via time.LoadLocation\(TimeZone\). The returned time carries the spec's location. ok=false when no future occurrence exists \(at in the past\).

<a name="TimingSpec.UnmarshalJSON"></a>
### func \(\*TimingSpec\) UnmarshalJSON

	func (t *TimingSpec) UnmarshalJSON(data []byte) error

UnmarshalJSON parses a spec whose kind is either the contracted snake\_case wire form \("at"\) or the legacy capitalized constant \("TimingOneShot" — written by builds before the JSON contract landed\). An unrecognized kind fails with ErrTimingUnsupported.

<a name="TimingSpec.Validate"></a>
### func \(\*TimingSpec\) Validate

	func (t *TimingSpec) Validate() error

Validate enforces kind\-specific input rules and the bounded RFC5545 profile. Out\-of\-profile constructs are rejected with a typed error, never silently mapped onto a wrong schedule.
